name: Ultrasonium
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.
one_liner: Metal manufacturing, faster, cheaper, and more versatile.

founders.title: Founder/CEO
founders.founder_bio: Founder & CEO of Ultrasonium. Inventor, physicist, and engineer with a PhD in EECS from MIT, with research spanning quantum computing, cryogenics, plasma research, signal processing, hardware control, and advanced manufacturing. First author of a Nature Physics publication in collaboration with MIT Lincoln Laboratory under IARPA and DoD programs. Former researcher at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. BA in Physics from UC Berkeley.

founders.title: Founder
founders.founder_bio:
Founder & VP, Engineering at Ultrasonium

Started my R&D career working at national labs by age 15. I have contributed to the ITER fusion reactor and CERN through labs at NHFML and LBNL. I have led teams of fabricators and designers in both research and industry. I am passionate about hard tech and moving groundbreaking research ideas into real products. 

I lead the Ultrasonium team on the novel and cutting edge technology we implement in our manufacturing process.

founders.title: Founder
founders.founder_bio: Founder & Chief Scientific Officer at Ultrasonium. PhD candidate on leave from MIT researching novel metal matrix materials and 3D printed metal heat treatments under NSF GRFP, MIT UCEM, GEM, and .406 Venture fellowship programs. Previously at Argonne National Laboratory working on 3D printed steel. Led metal melt pool simulations for NASA-funded multi-university project. Patent holder and publisher on metal printing. MS in Mechanical Engineering from MIT, BS from University of South Carolina.

founders.title: Founder
founders.founder_bio: Founder & Chief Research Officer of Ultrasonium. Former founder of the DOE-funded nuclear energy startup Bay State Energy and inventor of the Nuclear Thermoelectric Generator. Studied physics and computer science at Boston University. First hire at Phase3D - built and commercialized metals manufacturing technology deployed across NASA, USAF, and companies across four continents. Former metals manufacturing research engineer at Argonne National Laboratory. Dropped out of mech-e grad program.

launches.title: Ultrasonium: Shaping the Future of Metal Manufacturing
launches.tagline: We make the world’s most difficult metal parts faster, cheaper, and more versatile.
launches.body:
**The problem**

The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, robots, etc., are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and limited in the alloys and geometries they can process.

**What we built**

Ultrasonium has invented a new method to make these critical parts. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part comes out, controlled by a Physical AI layer and novel control processes.

We produce near-net-shape complex metal parts up to 15× faster, 75% cheaper, and with far greater alloy versatility than conventional manufacturing methods, at scale in the U.S.

<https://youtu.be/5REHWdzDAhk>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113464&key=user_uploads/3735756/dbd12c5d-1203-4e50-9939-980a218df45a)

**Why now / why us**

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, defense, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can’t be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has worked on some of the most difficult engineering systems in the world, including quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and advanced aerospace alloy processing. Between the four of us, we have backgrounds in physics, metallurgy, advanced manufacturing, controls, hardware, and commercialization.

Jack Qiu (CEO) completed his PhD in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT and published pioneering quantum computing work in Nature Physics. Chris Carter (CSO) left to join Ultrasonium during the 5th year of his PhD program at MIT after more than six years of research in state-of-the-art metallurgy and materials processing. Alexander Urbanski (Chief Research Officer) previously founded a DOE-funded nuclear startup and was the first hire at Phase3D, where he built and commercialized metal manufacturing monitoring technology. Hunter Brown (VP, Engineering) began working at national labs when he was 15, studied physics at UC Berkeley, and contributed to the ITER fusion reactor.
